results.fact: obj_haz lists hazards belonging to a different approach (Quien Sabe Glacier crevasses, Boston Basin bears) that don't apply to this route's actual Cascade Pass/Sahale Arm/Horseshoe Basin line
results.evidence: The Quien Sabe entry is explicitly conditional ('if approaching via the Quien Sabe Glacier'), and a Boston Basin / Quien Sabe Glacier / Boston-Sahale col approach to Buckner is a documented alternate way in (the row's own partner_requirements.approachTime names 'Sahale Arm or Boston Basin'). seasonal_hazards and hazards describe the main Sahale Arm line; the obj_haz items qualify the alternate approach, so these are two genuine options, not a contradiction.

results.correct_value: Sahale Glacier Camp to the Cascade Pass Trailhead is about 5.9 mi one way (the 9.6 figure is the same distance in km, mislabelled as miles)
results.evidence: One trail guide gives Sahale Glacier Camp as 5.9 mi (9.5 km) one way from the Cascade Pass trailhead with 3,940 ft gain (3.7 mi to the pass plus 2.2 mi up the Arm). WTA gives 12.0 mi round trip / 4,000 ft to the camp area, i.e. ~6 mi each way. The row's own waypoint (5.9) and approach text (5.9 mi) agree; descent_text's 9.6 is the km value, and the itinerary's 5.5 mi days understate the same leg.

results.fact: Season window: `season`/itinerary.cal say Jul-Sep, but best_season/seasonal_guidance/pro_tips say the route is best (and conditions degrade badly by high summer) in Late May-early July
results.evidence: No two independent sources state a face-specific window. SummitPost's peak page gives July-September as the optimum for the mountain generally (after avalanche danger); a guide service lists March-October; dated ascents found run from March (snowy spring) through May 14, July 4 and July 19, and one late-season report says the face was nearly melted out in August. That loosely supports 'earlier is better' but not the specific Late May-early July window, so no patch.

results.fact: Starting trailhead: approach/approach_variants/itinerary/timing all say Boston Basin Trailhead, but approach_logistics and the entire waypoint chain document the Cascade Pass Trailhead / Sahale Arm approach instead
results.correct_value: The standard approach starts at the Boston Basin Trailhead (Quien Sabe Glacier, then Sharkfin Col or around Boston Peak onto the Boston Glacier); the Cascade Pass / Sahale Arm line is the alternate way in and the usual exit.
results.evidence: A guide service's route page starts at the Boston Basin Trailhead (3,200 ft), climbs the Quien Sabe Glacier and gets around Boston Peak onto the Boston Glacier, then exits via Horseshoe Basin to the Cascade Pass trailhead. Independent trip reports (July 2014, November 2012, a ski descent) all start from the Boston Basin lot and cross Sharkfin Col onto the Boston Glacier. The patches correct the two waypoint texts that call Boston Basin the 'alternate'/'variant'. STILL OPEN: approach_logistics.trailhead and its coordinates, and the waypoint pins, still describe the Cascade Pass Trailhead. That name matches those coordinates, and moving coordinates is pin work outside this pass, so it is left for a pin repair.

results.evidence: Sources confirm the CJ Couloir line climbs from a terminal moraine up remnant glacier ice under the Sill hanging glacier, which sheds ice and rock and breaks up mid-to-late season. That undercuts seasonal_hazards' flat 'no glacier travel'. But no source describes crevasses on this route specifically, so neither the 'N/A' nor obj_haz's crevasse line has two sources behind it. No patch.

results.fact: distance to the East Ridge/col area
results.evidence: Sources agree the couloir approach is a short walk down the road, a river crossing (~20 min) and about 3,000 ft of booting to the C-J col, but none gives a mileage. The row's own trailhead and summit pins sit only ~1.4 km apart, so the itinerary's 5.7 mi per day (and the 11+ mi round trip / dist_km 18.35) cannot describe the couloir approach its notes narrate; they may come from the Cascade Pass / Mixup Arm variant. A Doug's Direct trip reports ~14 mi over three days by a longer line. Without two sources for the couloir mileage, no patch is written.

results.fact: bivy list includes Boston Basin lower/upper camps and Sahale Glacier Camp, which do not serve the CJ Couloir / East Ridge line
results.evidence: The Boston Basin lower and upper camps and Sahale Glacier Camp are regional Cascade River Road camps that do not serve this route. Johannesburg Camp near the trailhead and Pelton Basin (for the Mixup Arm variant) plausibly do. Left for the catalog-wide bivy class.

results.fact: Northwest Forest Pass requirement at Pyramid Lake trailhead
results.correct_value: No parking pass is needed at the Pyramid Lake trailhead (NPS land); an NPS backcountry permit is needed only to camp.
results.evidence: WTA's Pyramid Lake page lists Parking Pass/Entry Fee: None. The NPS North Cascades fees page says there are no trailhead or parking fees for trails that begin on NPS land, and that the Northwest Forest Pass applies at adjacent USFS trailheads. The Pyramid Lake trailhead is an NPS (Ross Lake NRA) trailhead. All three copies of the stale pass claim (gear, trailhead waypoint directions, approach) are corrected.
